title: Calibration acceptance micrometrics harness for FP8/INT8
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Build an automated accuracy validation harness that validates quantization profiles (FP8 and INT8) end-to-end for model onboarding and release gating. The harness must: 1) run calibration workflows against configurable calibration tables and collect per-layer activation statistics; 2) execute a curated set of 'micrometrics' — compact, high-signal checks (token-level perplexity delta, normalized logit-diff, embedding cosine drift, instruction-following exact-match, and safety/sanity heuristics) — across golden prompt partitions; 3) produce deterministic artifact bundles (replayable seeds, inputs, golden outputs, raw logits) for forensic replay; 4) evaluate against configurable pass/fail gates that support multi-metric rules (e.g., allow small embedding drift if token perplexity delta < X); and 5) integrate results into CI and the Redwood Console for telemetry and auditor-friendly export (CSV/JSON + links to artifacts).

Design constraints & acceptance criteria: harness runs in <6h for a full nightly suite on a 4-GPU Dedicated runner or within CI short-run mode in ~20m (subsampled prompts); results must include per-model/per-profile pass/fail, top-10 failure cases, and suggested mitigation tags (increase calibration samples, use per-channel quant, raise precision for critical layers). Golden prompt set must cover: instruction-following, code, multi-turn chat, summarization, and domain-specific seeds (finance, healthcare), with controlled randomness and stratified sampling. Pass/fail gates are configurable via YAML in repo and exposed in Console UI for rollout policies.

Trade-offs discussed: sample set size vs. speed (we will maintain two modes: fast smoke and full nightly). Using stricter micro-metrics reduces false negatives but increases human triage. We chose micrometrics over heavy end-to-end evals for nightly gating to keep costs predictable; full downstream evals remain part of release candidate checks.

Implementation notes: three components — runner (calibration + inference driver), comparator (metrics, thresholds, per-layer sensitivity scanner), and reporter (artifact bundle + Console upload + CI annotations). Shared libraries will reuse existing quant-profiling code from runtime and telemetry hooks. Tests must include seeded stochastic perturbations to detect brittle gates. Data retention: store only metadata and compressed artifacts for 90 days unless flagged for incident review.

Integration points: 1) CI gating for model onboarding PRs (fail build on P0 regressions); 2) Canary pipeline for rolling quantized model into Dedicated; 3) Console dashboard and alerts for regression spikes; 4) Ops runbook for triage with links to artifacts and suggested fixes.

Deliverables: harness code in infra/quant-harness repo, YAML-based gate config, golden prompt manifest, nightly job config (k8s cron), Console wiring for pass/fail, and a short runbook.
